findings.title: Platform Allocation and Network Flow vs Local Safety
findings.summary: SmartRail may propose network optimization platform changes that conflict with local safety, capacity constraints, or blocked platforms, requiring station managers to have veto or challenge authority.
findings.unresolved_question: Who has ultimate authority to override platform allocation disputes between local safety constraints and network optimization algorithms?
findings.rationale: Both sources address the tension between central network optimization and local platform safety/overcrowding, highlighting a direct operational conflict.

findings.title: Division of Authority for Platform Changes and Major Actions
findings.summary: Clear boundaries are needed between local operational authority for single train adjustments and central authorization required for major line-wide re-shuffles and station closures.
findings.rationale: These discoveries complement each other by outlining the spectrum of authority delegation between local and central control.

findings.title: Automated PA Announcement Capabilities and Error Handling
findings.summary: Uncertainty surrounds whether the automated PA system supports ad-hoc typing or pre-recorded messages, and how the system prevents or corrects panic-inducing announcement inaccuracies.
findings.unresolved_question: Can staff broadcast ad-hoc or pre-recorded messages, and does the system feature automated verification for announcements?
findings.rationale: Both findings focus on the functionality and risk profile of automated passenger announcements.

findings.title: Local Control of Station Displays and Messaging
findings.summary: It is unclear if station displays are entirely network-controlled or if local staff can utilize portions of displays for local operational or informational messages.
findings.unresolved_question: Can local staff override sections of network-controlled station displays to publish local operational messages?
findings.rationale: Unique finding regarding local management of customer-facing visual displays.

findings.title: Direct Incident Entry and Infrastructure Repair Loop Closure
findings.summary: Staff require capabilities to directly log facility outages and incidents into SmartRail, alongside a defined workflow to ensure maintenance issues are resolved and status is updated.
findings.unresolved_question: What is the formal workflow to close the loop on reported infrastructure failures and update their operational status?
findings.rationale: Combines direct incident logging with the lifecycle maintenance tracking and loop closure requirements.

findings.title: Tiered Incident Management Workflows
findings.summary: It is unspecified how SmartRail manages and distinguishes between varying levels of local incidents, such as minor platform spills versus major security alerts.
findings.unresolved_question: Does SmartRail contain distinct tiered incident management workflows for varying levels of local severity?
findings.rationale: Unique finding addressing severity-based workflow categorizations for local incidents.

findings.title: Local Offline Resilience and Connectivity Continuity
findings.summary: The system must provide a robust offline mode with backup power support to maintain core local functionality if network connections or power fail during major disruptions.
findings.unresolved_question: What core functionality can be maintained locally via backup power and offline cache if network connectivity is completely severed?
findings.rationale: Unique resilience requirement focusing on complete loss of local infrastructure connectivity.

findings.title: Granular Disruption Information Requirements for Staff
findings.summary: Staff require precise operational details during disruptions—such as affected trains, recovery plans, alternative transport locations, and resolution times—rather than generic delay notices.
findings.rationale: Represents a clear functional expectation for disruption communication tools.

findings.title: Integration with Local Security Systems
findings.summary: SmartRail needs integration with local security assets including CCTV and access control to support effective station incident response.
findings.rationale: Unique integration requirement concerning physical security systems.

findings.title: Automatic Ingestion of Local Context in Network Algorithms
findings.summary: There is an implicit assumption that network-wide optimization solutions must automatically incorporate local station context, density, and safety metrics without requiring manual intervention.
findings.unresolved_question: To what extent can network optimization algorithms ingest real-time local station density metrics automatically?
findings.rationale: Highlights a major scope tension regarding automated data ingestion versus manual oversight.
